Invited Speakers

All speakers listed below are confirmed.

Together they represent substantial institutional and geographic diversity, with a balanced mix of junior and senior researchers.

Mihaela van der Schaar John Humphrey Plummer Professor of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence and Medicine
University of Cambridge

“WIP”

Mihaela van der Schaar leads the van der Schaar Lab at Cambridge and founded the Cambridge Centre for AI in Medicine (CCAIM). A Fellow of the Royal Society (2024) and IEEE Fellow (2009), she is recognised as the most-cited female AI researcher in the UK. Her honours include the Johann Anton Merck Award (2024), the Oon Prize on Preventative Medicine, and an NSF CAREER Award. She holds 35 US patents, has contributed to over 45 international standards, and was a Turing Fellow at the Alan Turing Institute from 2016–2024.

Yali Du Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) in AI
King's College London

“WIP”

Yali Du heads the Distributed AI Group and leads the Cooperative AI Lab at King's College London. A Turing Fellow and ELLIS member, her research focuses on cooperative and safe multi-agent learning, human–AI coordination, and value alignment. She received the AAAI New Faculty Highlights Award and was named a KAUST Rising Star in AI (2023). Dr Du serves as Senior Area Chair for AAMAS and Area Chair for NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, and IJCAI.

Giorgia Ramponi Assistant Professor in AI for Cyber-Physical Systems
University of Zurich

“WIP”

Giorgia Ramponi is an Assistant Professor in AI for Cyber-Physical Systems at the University of Zurich. Her research spans reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and multi-agent systems. Prior to her current role, she was a Google Brain-sponsored postdoctoral researcher at the ETH AI Center, working with Niao He and Andreas Krause. She holds a PhD (with honours) in Information Technology from Politecnico di Milano (2021), supervised by Marcello Restelli.
